messages:

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Proposed revised termination & auto-renew mechanics for ACME PO

Hi Jared / Emily —

Following today's redline pass, legal and I sketched an alternative to the single 60‑day opt‑out that I think balances your operational predictability with Acme's pilot flexibility. Attached: ACME_Redlines_Term_20270502.docx and a short runbook (runbook_termination_playbook.pdf) that explains the post‑termination handoffs. Summary below: 

- Tiered notice windows: pilot seats = 30 days, multi‑year production commitments = 90 days; mid‑term pilots that convert get 60 days notice.
- Auto‑renew: rolling 12‑month renewals unless either party gives the applicable tier notice prior to renewal window.
- Termination for convenience (TFC): scaled exit fee based on remaining committed term (cap = 3 months of average MRR). Pilot customers who provide 30+ days notice are exempt from TFC; smaller pilots get a pro‑rated credit.
- Soft‑sunset & data egress: Redwood will keep a read‑only export endpoint for 60 days post‑termination (logs and KV cache excluded). Customer has option to trigger a one‑time extended export (up to 120 days) for a nominal fee. We will also offer an escrowed export if required.

We think this language reduces cliff events for both sides and gives Acme time to migrate without a hard outage. If Acme prefers a shorter production notice, tell us the target and Marissa (legal) can try to bridge.

Action items:
- Please review the attached redlines and call out any non‑starter items.
- If you want language we can drop directly into the order form, say so and Ben will prepare the pricing/redline markups.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call tomorrow if you prefer.

—
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: Proposed revised termination & auto-renew mechanics for ACME PO

Sofia —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. A couple quick points from procurement/ops at Acme after a brief internal sync: 

1) Production notice: 90 days feels long for our procurement cycle. Can you do 60 days for production commitments instead of 90? That would align with our renewal calendar.
2) Pilot TFC fee: we'd like Redwood to waive any termination‑for‑convenience fee for pilot accounts (30 seat / 3 month pilots). Pilots are low‑risk and we need the ability to pause without penalties to evaluate.
3) Soft‑sunset: the 60‑day read‑only export window is acceptable, but please confirm whether logs/usage reporting will be retained for the same period (we need billing reconciliation). If not, we need an SLA guaranteeing 7 days notice before log purge.

I've attached our counter redlines (Acme_counter_redlines_20270502.docx) that call out the points above. If Redwood can accept pilot fee waivers and 60‑day production notice, this should be straightforward to finalize.

Happy to jump on a short call Tuesday to close.

—
Jared Lee

Sofia —

Nice framing. I reviewed Jared's counterpoints and propose the following compromise language we can offer to Acme: 

1) Notice windows: Pilot = 30 days; Converted pilots / small production = 60 days; Standard production (multi‑year commits) = 75 days. Rationale: 75 days gives Redwood a slightly longer planning window while staying closer to Acme's 60 day request.

2) TFC mechanics: For pilots (<= 3 months / <= 50 seats) Redwood will waive TFC if Customer provides >= 30 days notice. For other tiers, TFC is pro‑rated: (remaining months / 12) * 3 months of MRR capped at 3 months.

3) Soft‑sunset & logs: Redwood keeps billing/usage records for 90 days post‑termination and provides a 7‑day pre‑purge notice for logs. Read‑only export endpoint is available for 60 days; Customer may request a one‑time extended export (up to 120 days) subject to a small fee.

I've drafted a snippet you can insert into the OF and MSA; see legal_snippet_redlines.txt attached. Ben — can you confirm if accepting pilot waiver triggers any pricing adjustment we need to route through finance? If so, please prepare the credit language so we can include it in the DocuSign package.

If Acme signs off on these points I'll push the snippet to the order form and share the DocuSign link.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachment: legal_snippet_redlines.txt
